text:
Alice M.: :rotating_light: quick heads-up — found what looks like a KMS IV fragment in a staging log backup (gs://staging-logs/backups/2026-03-22.log). not full ciphertext but an apparent base64 chunk.
Ben S.: can you paste the exact line?
Alice M.: line ~1245. pasted snippet: `..payload.., iv: \"QkFTRTY0SUZfR1JfKg==\", meta: {...}`. looks like a short iv field.
Carla (infra): hmm. that base64 decodes to 16 bytes (prob AES IV). could be noisy but we should treat as exposed material.
Dave P.: do we know which service wrote that log?
Alice M.: backup agent on staging (service account: svc-backup-staging@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com) wrote the file during scheduled snapshot.
Erin (prod): tagging legal & partners later if partner data impacted. for now we need containment + rotation.
Ben S.: immediate steps I suggest: 1) snapshot list of affected buckets, 2) revoke the svc acc key used to push backups, 3) rotate KMS wrap key(s) used for those backups, 4) kick off a scan for similar base64 patterns.
Carla (infra): agreed. I'll disable the backup agent push and rotate the CI deploy key for the agent. doing RBAC check now to see who can read that bucket.
SecurityBot: automated alert: audit log shows 3 reads of that object from IPs 35.**** within last 7 days.
Alice M.: anyone seen matching KMS key usage spikes around 2026-03-22T02:xxZ?
Ben S.: brief look at KMS metrics: wrap/unwrap for key projects/redwood-kms/keys/wrap-backup shows a 12% spike at 02:18Z (matches backup window).
Dave P.: so likely the IV fragment ended up in application logs before encryption or after?
Carla (infra): two possibilities: 1) backup tool logs the serialization payload (bad) containing the IV, 2) logging library base64-encodes some binary and logs it. need to check agent code quickly.
Ben S.: I'll grep the agent repo for `.iv` or `base64` logging. quick search:
```
$ git grep -n "iv" infra/backup-agent || true
infra/backup-agent/src/serialize.go:124: log.Debugf("payload iv=%s", base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(iv))
```
Ben S.: yep. there's an explicit debug log that prints IV in staging builds. looks like debug-level logs leaked into backups.
Erin (prod): oof. is that only in staging build?
Ben S.: code shows conditional on env DEBUG=true which was accidentally true in the staging deploy.
Alice M.: action list (short): 1) remove backups that contain the fragment, 2) rotate KMS wrap key(s), 3) rotate svc-account creds used by the agent, 4) tighten RBAC and audit export, 5) patch agent to stop logging IVs, 6) re-run scans and provide partner notice if PII touched.
Carla (infra): I'm on (1) and (3) now — nuking the most recent backups and revoking short-lived keys. leaving audit trail. doing `gsutil rm -r gs://staging-logs/backups/2026-03-22*` now.
InfraBot: scheduled delete job queued (job id: jd-20260322-17). object versioning note: bucket has versioning ON, previous versions retained.
Carla (infra): noted — will trigger retention-lift on that prefix to allow immediate purge via Object Lifecycle with `--force` flag and escalate to GCS support if needed.
Ben S.: on (2) KMS rotation — what's the wrap key name?
Dave P.: wrap key is `projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/wrap-backups-v1`. we should create wrap-backups-v2 and rewrap any ciphertext that needs rewrapping.
Alice M.: timeline: rotate now, rewrap non-binary blobs where possible, but encrypted backups should be re-encrypted as we re-run backups. for any existing ciphertext we may need to double-wrap or revoke the old key.
Erin (prod): Legal: please capture scope of data in that bucket. I will pull a quick sample for PII fields while you handle infra.
Ben S.: scanning step: I'll run a pattern scan across last 90 days for base64-looking tokens and `iv:` patterns.
Ben S.: `gsutil cat gs://staging-logs/backups/* | grep -n "iv:" | sed -n '1,200p'`
Ben S.: kicked off scan, ETA ~8m.
SecurityBot: automated audit export: bucket access logs forwarded to audit-exports project. generating report now.
Alice M.: RBAC changes: we need to tighten READ to only ops team for that bucket and rotate any ACL grants to service accounts. Carla, can you list current IAM bindings?
Carla (infra): current bindings: storage.objectViewer: [svc-backup-staging@..., devs@redwood-inference, infra-oncall@...] — I'll remove `devs@` and require IAM role via group `backup-operators`.
Dave P.: also bump logging level in the deployment manifest to `INFO` and ensure DEBUG not set anywhere in staging values.
Carla (infra): will push a quick patch to helm values and trigger rollback.
Ben S.: for KMS rotation, propose: 1) create wrap-backups-v2, 2) update encryption context in backup agent to use v2, 3) force immediate re-run of backups under maintenance window, 4) mark v1 as pending destroy after 48 hours once no active unwraps observed.
Alice M.: risk call: any consumer that has stored raw IVs but not keys — an attacker with object-level read + old ciphertext + wrap key compromise could decrypt. since we don't believe wrap key compromised, we still rotate to reduce blast radius.
Erin (prod): Partner coordination: do we need to notify partner X? Not immediately. first confirm if any partner-derived records in those backups. I'll prioritize sample scan.
Ben S.: scan results first batch: 7 matching objects (small). sharing list to #sec-incidents DM.
Alice M.: next immediate steps owners: Carla -> purge + RBAC change + helm patch. Ben -> run full scan + KMS rotation play. Dave -> prepare rewrap scripts and coop with Carla for deploy. Erin -> partner/legal triage + PII sample. Me (Alice) -> coordinate rotation timeline and postmortem stub.
Carla (infra): started RBAC change: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=group:backup-operators@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/storage.objectViewer` then removed `devs@` binding.
Ben S.: KMS key create in progress: `gcloud kms keys create wrap-backups-v2 --keyring=backups --location=global --purpose=encryption`
InfraBot: KMS key wrap-backups-v2 created (id: k-20260322-02).
Dave P.: rewrap helper (local):
```
for obj in $(cat rewrap-list.txt); do
  gsutil cp gs://staging-logs/$obj - | ./rewrap_tool --from-key=wrap-backups-v1 --to-key=wrap-backups-v2 | gsutil cp - gs://staging-logs-rewrapped/$obj
done
```
Dave P.: will run in maintenance window 2026-03-22T06:00Z.
Alice M.: assign follow-ups in ticket INFSEC-423. please add detailed logs and audit export links.
Erin (prod): thumbs-up. I'll prepare partner blurb (if needed) and hold until scan completes.
Ben S.: scan done — only staging internal backups affected, no partner PII detected in sample.
Alice M.: good. mark communication as internal-only for now.
Carla (infra): purge completed for primary object versions; opened GCS support ticket to expedite version deletion for older versions (ticket: GCS-5567).
SecurityBot: reminder: update KMS key rotation schedule in the security playbook and add a check to CI to ensure DEBUG!=true in env for production & staging helm values.
Alice M.: agreed. I'll add the CI gate.
Ben S.: tl;dr: leakage via debug logging, not KMS crypto compromise. containment done, rotations initiated, RBAC tightened, follow-up tickets created.
Dave P.: postmortem volunteers? I'll take the infra section. Ben you take detection/metrics. Alice will own overall.
Alice M.: thanks all. closing thread once tickets updated. :lock: :thumbsup:
